findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives undefined when the array is empty or null, and the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar. Previously the code used `?.`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Team member calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. Collective hosts' calendars are silently ignored, which is exactly the scenario this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Reschedule merge only deletes the first host's old calendar event
findings.body: When `newBookingId` is set, only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`) is deleted. With multiple hosts there are several references, so the other hosts keep stale events on their calendars after a reschedule.

findings.title: Recurring cancel repeats the full delete for every reference and ignores other hosts' credentials
findings.body: Inside the per-reference loop, the recurring branch iterates over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and all updated bookings. It does this once for each reference, so the same deletes run multiple times. It also only uses the first `_calendar` ref and the organizer's credentials, so other hosts' recurring events are never deleted.

findings.title: Fallback lookup can never match
findings.body: The `find` that compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match anything. The previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost. Update and delete then go to undefined in update, or to `primary` in delete, instead of the configured calendar. The same issue appears in deleteEvent at line 317.

findings.title: Inverted slug condition for org creation
findings.body: The original code set `slug` when billing was disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). The new code sets it when billing is enabled, which bypasses the paid slug request flow. When billing is disabled, organizations are now created without a slug. This change is unrelated to the PR and is a regression.

findings.title: E2E expectations inconsistent with new array type
findings.body: BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The payload is now an array or null, depending on the code path. BOOKING_REJECTED was changed to `[]`, so these expectations should be checked for consistency.
